title: Accelerating Graph-Based RAG Retrieval via Locality-Aware Device-Cloud Collaboration

problem.claim: The retrieval stage of RAG increasingly dominates end-to-end latency as knowledge bases scale, limiting system responsiveness.

gap.claim: Per-user query locality in RAG workloads is a previously underexplored property.

contributions.claim: The paper identifies and empirically validates strong per-user query locality in RAG workloads.
Lever is a locality-aware collaborative retrieval framework that uses query locality to accelerate graph-based RAG retrieval.
Lever maintains compact personalized on-device subgraph indexes and uses adaptive resampling to align them with evolving query patterns.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on multiple RAG benchmarks reportedly show significantly reduced retrieval latency and improved throughput.
The reported retrieval-quality results indicate preservation of retrieval quality while improving efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG uses external knowledge to ground language models for knowledge-intensive tasks.
Scaling knowledge bases makes retrieval a growing source of end-to-end latency.
Users' RAG queries reportedly concentrate on small subsets of the knowledge space.
Lever exploits query locality through personalized device-side subgraph indexes and adaptive resampling.
Experiments reportedly show lower latency, higher throughput, and preserved retrieval quality.

source_observation.claim: Individual users' queries may concentrate on a small subset of a large knowledge space.

interpretation.claim: User-specific locality can be exploited as an additional systems-level optimization signal for retrieval.

application.claim: Maintain compact personalized local indexes that guide traversal of a global retrieval structure.

exception.claim: Local indexes may need adaptive resampling when users' query patterns evolve.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark names, dataset sizes, or quantitative latency and throughput improvements.
The abstract does not detail the device-cloud coordination protocol or adaptive resampling algorithm.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported experimental results.
